questions.question_text: Are you automatically exempt from English language proficiency requirements if you were born in Australia?
options: Yes, being born in Australia is sufficient
No, you must also have an assessable qualification undertaken in English
Only if you provide a birth certificate
Only if your parents are Australian citizens
questions.explanation: Being born in an English-speaking country does not automatically exempt you; you still need to demonstrate your proficiency through an assessable qualification.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a commonly accepted English proficiency test by many institutions?
options: IELTS
A standard school essay
A verbal interview with a teacher
Your high school report card only
questions.explanation: IELTS (International English Language Testing System) is a widely recognized test for proving English proficiency for university entry.

questions.question_text: Are you automatically exempt from English language proficiency requirements simply because you were born in Australia?
options: Yes, if you were born in Australia you are always exempt
No, you must also hold an assessable qualification undertaken in English
Yes, provided you speak English at home
Only if you attended a private school
questions.explanation: Being born in Australia does not automatically satisfy English language proficiency requirements; you must also possess an assessable qualification (such as Year 12) undertaken in English.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a commonly accepted English proficiency test by many Australian institutions?
options: The driving theory test
The International English Language Testing System (IELTS)
A casual interview with a friend
Your high school report card from a non-English country
questions.explanation: IELTS (Academic) is widely recognized by Australian tertiary institutions as proof of English language proficiency.

questions.question_text: What happens if your English language proficiency test is not listed among the commonly accepted tests?
options: You cannot apply to any university
UAC will automatically approve it
You should write to the Admissions Office at each institution for a determination
You must take the test again until you pass
questions.explanation: If your specific test is not pre-approved, you should contact the relevant institutions directly with supporting documentation so they can determine if your qualification is acceptable.

questions.question_text: What is the requirement regarding English language proficiency for nursing and midwifery courses?
options: There are no specific requirements
A high level of English proficiency must be demonstrated
You only need to prove proficiency after graduating
You must have lived in an English-speaking country for at least 10 years
questions.explanation: Due to accreditation standards, nursing and midwifery applicants must demonstrate a high level of English language proficiency as part of the application process.

questions.question_text: If your English proficiency test is not listed among the commonly accepted tests, what should you do?
options: Assume it is not accepted and stop applying
Write to the Admissions Office at each institution you are applying to for a decision
Upload it to UAC and wait for an automatic update
Ask your friends if they think it is equivalent
questions.explanation: UAC cannot decide on proficiency on behalf of institutions; you must contact the institutions directly to see if they will accept your specific test.

questions.question_text: What happens if you are a Year 12 student born in a non-English-speaking country?
options: You are automatically disqualified
You must provide proof of proficiency through your Year 12 results
You must take an extra test before applying
You are immediately granted an exemption
questions.explanation: All applicants born in non-English-speaking countries must provide proof of proficiency, which is usually satisfied by their Year 12 qualification results.
